records.literal_gloss: For look, they have gone from devastation; Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them; desirable [things] of their silver, nettle will possess them; thorn [will be] in their tents.

en.L: For look, they have gone from destruction; \q Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them; \q their precious things of silver, nettles will possess them; \q thorns [will be] in their tents.
en.B: For look, even if they escape the destruction, \q Egypt will gather them in, and Memphis will bury them. \q Nettles will take over their treasures of silver, \q and thorns will grow in their tents.
en.R: Even if they escape when their land is destroyed, \q Egypt will gather them up, and they will be buried in Memphis. \q Weeds will grow over the silver things they love, \q and thorns will grow where their tents stood.

es.L: Porque he aquí, se han ido de la destrucción; \q Egipto los recogerá, Menfis los sepultará; \q sus objetos preciosos de plata, las ortigas los poseerán; \q espinos [habrá] en sus tiendas.
es.B: Porque aunque escapen de la destrucción, \q Egipto los recogerá, y Menfis los enterrará. \q Las ortigas se adueñarán de sus tesoros de plata, \q y los espinos crecerán en sus tiendas.
es.R: Aunque escapen cuando su tierra sea destruida, \q Egipto los recogerá, y serán enterrados en Menfis. \q La maleza crecerá sobre las cosas de plata que tanto aman, \q y los espinos crecerán donde estaban sus tiendas.

fr.L: Car voici, ils sont partis loin de la dévastation ; \q l’Égypte les rassemblera, Memphis les enterrera ; \q leurs objets précieux d’argent, les orties en prendront possession ; \q les épines [seront] dans leurs tentes.
fr.B: Car voici, même s’ils échappent à la dévastation, \q l’Égypte les recueillira et Memphis les enterrera. \q Les orties envahiront leurs trésors d’argent, \q et les épines pousseront dans leurs tentes.
fr.R: Même s’ils s’échappent quand leur pays sera détruit, \q l’Égypte les ramassera, et ils seront enterrés à Memphis. \q Les mauvaises herbes pousseront sur les objets d’argent qu’ils aiment, \q et les épines pousseront là où se dressaient leurs tentes.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, wamekwenda kutoka maangamizi; \q Misri itawakusanya, Memfisi itawazika; \q vitu vyao vya thamani vya fedha, mimea ya kuwasha itavimiliki; \q miiba [itakuwa] katika hema zao.
sw.B: Kwa maana tazama, hata wakiepuka maangamizi, \q Misri itawakusanya, na Memfisi itawazika. \q Mimea ya kuwasha itavifunika vitu vyao vya thamani vya fedha, \q na miiba itaota katika hema zao.
sw.R: Hata wakikimbia nchi yao inapoangamizwa, \q Misri itawakusanya, nao watazikwa huko Memfisi. \q Magugu yataota juu ya vitu vya fedha wanavyovipenda, \q na miiba itaota pale hema zao zilipokuwa.

vi.L: Vì kìa, chúng đã đi khỏi cảnh tàn phá; \q Ai Cập sẽ gom chúng lại, Mem-phít sẽ chôn chúng; \q những vật quý bằng bạc của chúng, cây tầm ma sẽ chiếm lấy; \q gai góc [sẽ mọc] trong các trại của chúng.
vi.B: Vì kìa, dù chúng thoát khỏi cảnh tàn phá, \q Ai Cập sẽ thu nhặt chúng, và Mem-phít sẽ chôn chúng. \q Cây tầm ma sẽ phủ lấp các bảo vật bằng bạc của chúng, \q và gai góc sẽ mọc trong các lều trại của chúng.
vi.R: Dù chúng thoát chạy khi xứ sở bị tàn phá, \q Ai Cập sẽ gom chúng lại, và chúng sẽ bị chôn tại Mem-phít. \q Cỏ dại sẽ mọc phủ những đồ bạc chúng yêu quý, \q và gai góc sẽ mọc nơi lều trại chúng từng dựng.

ko.L: 보라, 그들이 멸망을 피해 떠나갔으나, \q 이집트가 그들을 모으고 멤피스가 그들을 묻을 것이다. \q 그들의 은으로 된 귀한 것들은 쐐기풀이 차지하고, \q 그들의 장막에는 가시덤불이 [자랄 것이다].
ko.B: 보아라, 그들이 멸망을 피해 달아나도, \q 이집트가 그들을 거두어들이고 멤피스가 그들을 묻을 것이다. \q 그들의 귀한 은붙이는 쐐기풀이 뒤덮고, \q 그들의 장막에는 가시덤불이 자랄 것이다.
ko.R: 그들의 땅이 망할 때 그들이 피해 달아나더라도, \q 이집트가 그들을 거두어 가고, 그들은 멤피스에 묻힐 것이다. \q 그들이 아끼던 은붙이 위로 잡초가 자라고, \q 그들의 장막이 있던 자리에는 가시덤불이 자랄 것이다.

decisions.choice: look, they have gone from destruction: even if they flee the devastation
alternatives: look, they have gone to destruction
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past tense, but it pictures what is certain to come: they are already gone. "From destruction" means fleeing the devastation of the land. Escape will not save them: Egypt will be their grave.

decisions.choice: Memphis: the city of ancient Egypt known for its burial grounds
decisions.reason: Memphis, near modern Cairo, was one of Egypt's chief cities (Isaiah 19:13; Jeremiah 46:14), and the great cemeteries and pyramids of the Egyptian kings stood near it. Those who flee to Egypt will be gathered there only to be buried.

decisions.choice: their precious things of silver: their treasures, perhaps their silver idols
alternatives: their silver idols in particular
decisions.reason: The phrase means things of silver they valued. In 8:4 Hosea says that they made idols of their silver and gold, so the phrase may include them, but it can mean any treasure left behind in their homes.

decisions.choice: nettles and thorns in their tents: homes left empty and overgrown
decisions.reason: "Tents" is an old word for homes. When a land is emptied, weeds take it over (Isaiah 34:13). Their treasures and their houses will be left to the nettles.

decisions.choice: when their land is destroyed ... where their tents stood
decisions.reason: Readable says what the destruction is (the ruin of their land) and that the tents stand empty.

decisions.choice: "Menfis"
decisions.reason: The published Spanish form (Jeremiah 2:16).

source.text: בָּ֣אוּ׀יְמֵ֣י הַפְּקֻדָּ֗ה בָּ֚אוּ יְמֵ֣י הַשִׁלֻּ֔םיֵדְע֖וּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֱוִ֣יל הַנָּבִ֗יא מְשֻׁגָּע֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָר֔וּחַ עַ֚ל רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנְךָ֔ וְרַבָּ֖ה מַשְׂטֵמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Have come the days of the punishment; have come the days of the repayment; let know Israel. A fool [is] the prophet; mad [is] the man of the spirit, on account of the greatness of your iniquity, and great hostility.

en.L: The days of punishment have come; the days of repayment have come; \q let Israel know [it]! \q "The prophet [is] a fool; the man of the Spirit [is] mad!" \q because of the greatness of your iniquity, \q and great [is your] hostility.
en.B: The days of punishment have come; the days of repayment have come. \q Let Israel know it! \q "The prophet is a fool; the man of the Spirit is mad!" you say, \q because your guilt is so great \q and your hostility so deep.
en.R: The time of punishment has come. The time to pay Israel back has come. \q Let Israel understand this! \q You say, "The prophet is a fool! The man God's Spirit moves is crazy!" \q You say this because your sins are so many \q and your hatred is so great.

es.L: Han llegado los días del castigo; han llegado los días de la retribución; \q ¡que Israel [lo] sepa! \q «¡Necio [es] el profeta; loco el hombre del Espíritu!», \q por la grandeza de tu iniquidad, \q y grande [es tu] hostilidad.
es.B: Han llegado los días del castigo; han llegado los días de la retribución. \q ¡Que Israel lo sepa! \q «¡El profeta es un necio; el hombre del Espíritu está loco!», dices, \q porque tu culpa es tan grande \q y tan profunda tu hostilidad.
es.R: Ha llegado el tiempo del castigo. Ha llegado el tiempo de darle a Israel lo que merece. \q ¡Que Israel lo entienda! \q Tú dices: «¡El profeta es un necio! ¡El hombre a quien mueve el Espíritu de Dios está loco!». \q Lo dices porque tus pecados son tantos \q y tu odio es tan grande.

fr.L: Les jours du châtiment sont venus ; les jours de la rétribution sont venus ; \q qu’Israël [le] sache ! \q « Le prophète [est] fou ; l’homme de l’Esprit [est] insensé ! » \q à cause de la grandeur de ton iniquité, \q et grande [est ton] hostilité.
fr.B: Les jours du châtiment sont venus ; les jours de la rétribution sont venus. \q Qu’Israël le sache ! \q « Le prophète est fou ; l’homme de l’Esprit a perdu la raison ! » dis-tu, \q parce que ta faute est si grande \q et ton hostilité si profonde.
fr.R: Le temps de la punition est venu. Le temps de faire payer Israël est venu. \q Qu’Israël le comprenne ! \q Tu dis : « Le prophète est fou ! L’homme que l’Esprit de Dieu fait parler a perdu la tête ! » \q Tu dis cela parce que tes péchés sont si nombreux \q et ta haine si grande.

sw.L: Siku za adhabu zimekuja; siku za malipo zimekuja; \q Israeli na ajue [hilo]! \q "Nabii [ni] mpumbavu; mtu wa Roho [ana] wazimu!" \q kwa sababu ya wingi wa uovu wako, \q na [uadui wako ni] mkubwa.
sw.B: Siku za adhabu zimekuja; siku za malipo zimekuja. \q Israeli na ajue jambo hili! \q "Nabii ni mpumbavu; mtu wa Roho ana wazimu!" unasema, \q kwa sababu hatia yako ni kubwa mno \q na uadui wako ni mzito.
sw.R: Wakati wa adhabu umefika. Wakati wa kumlipiza Israeli umefika. \q Israeli na alielewe jambo hili! \q Unasema, "Nabii ni mpumbavu! Mtu anayeongozwa na Roho wa Mungu ana wazimu!" \q Unasema hivyo kwa sababu dhambi zako ni nyingi mno \q na chuki yako ni kubwa mno.

vi.L: Những ngày trừng phạt đã đến; những ngày báo trả đã đến; \q hãy để Y-sơ-ra-ên biết [điều đó]! \q "Nhà tiên tri [là] kẻ ngu dại; người của Thần Linh [là] kẻ điên!" \q vì sự gian ác lớn lao của ngươi, \q và sự thù nghịch [của ngươi] lớn lắm.
vi.B: Những ngày trừng phạt đã đến; những ngày báo trả đã đến. \q Y-sơ-ra-ên hãy biết điều đó! \q Ngươi nói: "Nhà tiên tri là kẻ ngu dại; người của Thần Linh là kẻ điên!" \q vì tội lỗi ngươi quá lớn \q và lòng thù nghịch của ngươi quá sâu.
vi.R: Thời trừng phạt đã đến. Thời báo trả Y-sơ-ra-ên đã đến. \q Y-sơ-ra-ên hãy hiểu rõ điều này! \q Ngươi nói: "Nhà tiên tri là đồ ngu! Người được Thần Linh của Đức Chúa Trời cảm động là kẻ điên!" \q Ngươi nói thế vì tội lỗi ngươi quá nhiều \q và lòng thù ghét của ngươi quá lớn.

ko.L: 벌 받을 날들이 왔고, 보복의 날들이 왔다. \q 이스라엘은 [이것을] 알아라! \q "예언자는 어리석은 자요, 영의 사람은 미친 자다!" \q 네 죄악이 크고, \q [네] 적대감이 크기 때문이다.
ko.B: 벌 받을 날이 왔다. 보복의 날이 왔다. \q 이스라엘은 이것을 알아라! \q 너희는 "예언자는 바보다. 영에 감동된 사람은 미쳤다!" 하고 말한다. \q 너희의 죄가 너무 크고, \q 너희의 적대감이 너무 깊기 때문이다.
ko.R: 벌을 받을 때가 왔다. 이스라엘에게 갚아 줄 때가 왔다. \q 이스라엘은 이것을 깨달아라! \q 너희는 "예언자는 바보다! 하나님의 영에 감동된 사람은 미쳤다!" 하고 말한다. \q 너희가 그렇게 말하는 것은 너희의 죄가 너무 많고, \q 너희의 미움이 너무 크기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: "The prophet is a fool": the people's mocking verdict on the prophet
alternatives: the prophet's own verdict on Israel's prophets, who have become fools
the punishment will drive the prophet out of his mind
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not mark who says these words. Read as the people's words, they are what Israel says of Hosea and prophets like him, because its guilt is so great and its hostility so deep. Israel's officers called a prophet "this madman" in 2 Kings 9:11, and Jeremiah 29:26 speaks of "every madman who prophesies". The words could also be Hosea's judgment on Israel's own prophets (4:5), who will be shown up as fools when the days of punishment come.

decisions.choice: the man of the Spirit: the inspired prophet
decisions.reason: The phrase is used only here. It describes a man moved by God's Spirit, as the Spirit came on the elders and on Saul when they prophesied (Numbers 11:25-29; 1 Samuel 10:6, 10). The parallel is "the prophet".

decisions.choice: punishment, repayment, hostility
decisions.reason: "Punishment" is the noun of the verb in verse 9 ("he will punish their sins"), God's coming to settle accounts. "Repayment" is the payment of what is owed. "Hostility" is a rare word, from the same root as satan ("adversary"); it returns in verse 8.

decisions.choice: you say
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who calls the prophet a fool, following m1. Literal marks the words as speech with quotation marks only.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity follows the wording settled for the prophets: "iniquity" at Literal, "guilt" at Balanced, "sin" at Readable.

decisions.choice: the people's verdict in « »; "tu", "dices" (tú)
decisions.reason: The mocking words are quoted speech inside the oracle, so they take Spanish quotation marks. The Hebrew "your" here is singular, Israel as one person, so Spanish uses tú.

decisions.choice: "el hombre del Espíritu"
decisions.reason: Capitalized, as the English, since the inspired prophet is moved by God's Spirit.

decisions.choice: "dis-tu" (B), "Tu dis" (R), singular
alternatives: "dites-vous"
decisions.reason: The English "you say" leaves the number open; the Hebrew "your iniquity" is singular, Israel addressed as one, so French says "tu".

source.text: צֹפֶ֥ה אֶפְרַ֖יִם עִם־אֱלֹהָ֑י נָבִ֞יא פַּ֤ח יָקוֹשׁ֙ עַל־כָּל־דְּרָכָ֔יו מַשְׂטֵמָ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: A watchman of Ephraim with my God [is] a prophet; a snare of a fowler [is] on all his ways, hostility in [the] house of his God.

en.L: The prophet [is] a watchman of Ephraim with my God; \q a fowler's snare [is] on all his ways, \q hostility in the house of his God.
en.B: The prophet is the watchman over Ephraim, with my God; \q yet a fowler's snare lies on all his paths, \q and hostility waits for him in the house of his God.
en.R: The prophet is a guard who watches over Ephraim for my God. \q But people set traps for him wherever he goes, \q and even in the house of his God they hate him.

es.L: Centinela de Efraín con mi Dios [es] el profeta; \q lazo de cazador [hay] en todos sus caminos, \q hostilidad en la casa de su Dios.
es.B: El profeta es el centinela de Efraín junto con mi Dios; \q pero en todos sus caminos hay un lazo de cazador, \q y en la casa de su Dios lo espera la hostilidad.
es.R: El profeta es un guardia que vigila a Efraín para mi Dios. \q Pero la gente le pone trampas dondequiera que va, \q y aun en la casa de su Dios lo odian.

fr.L: Le prophète [est] une sentinelle d’Éphraïm avec mon Dieu ; \q un piège d’oiseleur [est] sur toutes ses voies, \q l’hostilité dans la maison de son Dieu.
fr.B: Le prophète est la sentinelle d’Éphraïm, avec mon Dieu ; \q pourtant un piège d’oiseleur est tendu sur tous ses chemins, \q et l’hostilité l’attend dans la maison de son Dieu.
fr.R: Le prophète est une sentinelle qui veille sur Éphraïm pour mon Dieu. \q Mais les gens lui tendent des pièges partout où il va, \q et même dans la maison de son Dieu, on le déteste.

sw.L: Nabii [ni] mlinzi wa Efraimu pamoja na Mungu wangu; \q mtego wa mwindaji ndege [uko] juu ya njia zake zote, \q uadui katika nyumba ya Mungu wake.
sw.B: Nabii ni mlinzi juu ya Efraimu, pamoja na Mungu wangu; \q lakini mtego wa mwindaji ndege umetegwa katika njia zake zote, \q na uadui unamngoja katika nyumba ya Mungu wake.
sw.R: Nabii ni mlinzi anayemlinda Efraimu kwa ajili ya Mungu wangu. \q Lakini watu wanamtegea mitego kila aendako, \q na hata katika nyumba ya Mungu wake wanamchukia.

vi.L: Nhà tiên tri [là] người canh gác của Ép-ra-im cùng với Đức Chúa Trời của tôi; \q bẫy của kẻ bắt chim [giăng] trên mọi đường lối người, \q sự thù nghịch trong nhà Đức Chúa Trời của người.
vi.B: Nhà tiên tri là người canh gác Ép-ra-im, cùng với Đức Chúa Trời của tôi; \q thế mà bẫy của kẻ bắt chim giăng trên mọi nẻo đường người đi, \q và sự thù nghịch chờ người trong nhà Đức Chúa Trời của người.
vi.R: Nhà tiên tri là người canh gác, canh giữ Ép-ra-im cho Đức Chúa Trời của tôi. \q Nhưng người ta gài bẫy người ở khắp nơi người đến, \q và ngay trong nhà Đức Chúa Trời của người, họ cũng ghét người.

ko.L: 예언자는 나의 하나님과 함께 에브라임의 파수꾼이다. \q 새 사냥꾼의 올무가 그의 모든 길에 있고, \q 그의 하나님의 집에 적대감이 있다.
ko.B: 예언자는 나의 하나님과 함께 에브라임을 지키는 파수꾼이다. \q 그런데 그가 가는 길마다 새 사냥꾼의 올무가 놓여 있고, \q 그의 하나님의 집에서도 적대감이 그를 기다린다.
ko.R: 예언자는 나의 하나님을 위해 에브라임을 지키는 파수꾼이다. \q 그러나 사람들은 그가 가는 곳마다 덫을 놓고, \q 그의 하나님의 집에서까지 그를 미워한다.

decisions.choice: the prophet is a watchman over Ephraim, with my God
alternatives: Ephraim keeps watch beside my God, and the prophet finds a trap on all his ways
Ephraim, the watchman, is with my God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and hard: "watchman Ephraim with my God prophet". Read as here, the prophet is the lookout God has set over his people, as in Jeremiah 6:17 and Ezekiel 3:17, and he does that work together with God. Others read Ephraim as the one who watches, spying out the prophet or setting itself up as a rival lookout beside God. Either way, the rest of the verse shows the prophet hunted and hated by those he warns.

decisions.choice: a fowler's snare on all his ways: plots laid against the prophet wherever he goes
decisions.reason: A fowler caught birds with hidden traps (Psalm 91:3; 124:7). The people set traps for the prophet as a bird-catcher does.

decisions.choice: hostility in the house of his God
decisions.reason: "Hostility" picks up the end of verse 7. "The house of his God" may be the sanctuary where the prophet speaks, or the land and people of God, as in 8:1 and 9:15. Even there he meets hatred.

decisions.choice: my God: the prophet speaks
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, the prophet speaks of "my God". He sets God, whom he serves, against the people who oppose him.

decisions.choice: people set traps for him
decisions.reason: Readable says that the people set the traps, which the Hebrew leaves implied.

decisions.choice: "centinela"
decisions.reason: The watchman (tsofeh) is "centinela" at every level in these books, as the terms note sets; Readable says "guardia que vigila", as the English Readable explains.

decisions.choice: "sentinelle" at every level for the watchman
alternatives: "guetteur"
"gardien" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the prophets' watchman; "mon Dieu" is the prophet's own word, so it takes no deity_pronoun span.

source.text: הֶעְמִֽיקוּ־שִׁחֵ֖תוּ כִּימֵ֣י הַגִּבְעָ֑ה יִזְכּ֣וֹר עֲוֺנָ֔ם יִפְק֖וֹד חַטֹּאותָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They have made deep, they have acted corruptly, as [in the] days of Gibeah; he will remember their iniquity; he will punish their sins.

en.L: They have gone deep, they have acted corruptly, as [in] the days at Gibeah; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remember their iniquity; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will punish their sins.
en.B: They have sunk deep into corruption, as at Gibeah in days gone by. \q He will remember their guilt; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will punish their sins.
en.R: They have become as evil as the people of Gibeah were in the old days. \q God will remember the wrong they have done \q and make them pay for their sins.

es.L: Se han hundido, se han corrompido, como en los días de Guibeá; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recordará su iniquidad, \q castigará sus pecados.
es.B: Se han hundido en la corrupción, como en los días de Guibeá. \q Él recordará su culpa \q y castigará sus pecados.
es.R: Se han vuelto tan malvados como la gente de Guibeá en los tiempos antiguos. \q Dios recordará el mal que han hecho \q y les hará pagar por sus pecados.

fr.L: Ils ont creusé profond, ils se sont corrompus, comme [aux] jours de Guibea ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se souviendra de leur iniquité ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} punira leurs péchés.
fr.B: Ils se sont enfoncés dans la corruption, comme autrefois à Guibea. \q Il se souviendra de leur faute ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} punira leurs péchés.
fr.R: Ils sont devenus aussi mauvais que les gens de Guibea autrefois. \q Dieu se souviendra du mal qu’ils ont fait \q et leur fera payer leurs péchés.

sw.L: Wameingia ndani sana, wametenda kwa upotovu, kama [katika] siku za Gibea; \q atakumbuka uovu wao; \q atawaadhibu kwa dhambi zao.
sw.B: Wamezama sana katika upotovu, kama huko Gibea siku za zamani. \q Atakumbuka hatia yao; \q atawaadhibu kwa dhambi zao.
sw.R: Wamekuwa waovu kama watu wa Gibea walivyokuwa zamani. \q Mungu atakumbuka mabaya waliyoyatenda \q na kuwalipiza kwa dhambi zao.

vi.L: Chúng đã đi sâu, đã làm điều bại hoại, như [trong] những ngày tại Ghi-bê-a; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nhớ lại sự gian ác của chúng; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ thăm phạt tội lỗi chúng.
vi.B: Chúng đã chìm sâu trong sự bại hoại, như tại Ghi-bê-a thuở trước. \q Ngài sẽ nhớ lại tội lỗi chúng; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ trừng phạt tội của chúng.
vi.R: Chúng đã trở nên gian ác như dân Ghi-bê-a ngày xưa. \q Đức Chúa Trời sẽ nhớ lại những điều sai trái chúng đã làm \q và bắt chúng trả giá cho tội lỗi mình.

ko.L: 그들이 기브아의 시절처럼 깊이 타락했다. \q 그분께서 그들의 죄악을 기억하시고 \q 그들의 죄를 벌하실 것이다.
ko.B: 그들은 지난날 기브아에서처럼 타락에 깊이 빠졌다. \q 그분께서 그들의 죄악을 기억하시고 \q 그들의 죄를 벌하실 것이다.
ko.R: 그들은 옛날 기브아 사람들처럼 악해졌다. \q 하나님께서 그들이 저지른 잘못을 기억하시고 \q 그 죄의 값을 치르게 하실 것이다.

decisions.choice: they have deeply corrupted themselves
decisions.reason: Two verbs stand side by side: "they have made deep, they have acted corruptly". The first strengthens the second: they have sunk deep into corruption (compare Isaiah 31:6).

decisions.choice: the days of Gibeah: the outrage at Gibeah in Judges 19-21
alternatives: the beginning of Saul's kingship at Gibeah (1 Samuel 10:26; 15:34)
decisions.reason: At Gibeah in Benjamin the men of the town abused a Levite's concubine until she died, and Israel went to war against Benjamin to punish them (Judges 19-21). Those who saw it said that nothing like it had been done since Israel came up out of Egypt (Judges 19:30). Hosea says that Israel's corruption now runs as deep. He returns to Gibeah in 10:9, where the war fits Judges 20. Gibeah was also Saul's home and royal seat, and some take Hosea's word as a charge against the kingship (8:4; 13:10-11); but the crime and the war make Judges the likelier reference.

decisions.choice: he will remember their iniquity; he will punish their sins: the words of 8:13
decisions.reason: The same words close 8:13, and Jeremiah 14:10 repeats them of Judah. "Remember" means call to account, and the subject is God.

decisions.choice: the wording of Jeremiah 14:10
decisions.reason: The second half uses the wording already published for Jeremiah 14:10, which quotes these words: "he will remember their iniquity ... punish their sins" (Literal), "guilt" for iniquity (Balanced), and "remember the wrong they have done and make them pay for their sins" (Readable). Readable says "God" for "he".

decisions.choice: "recordará su iniquidad ... castigará sus pecados" (L) and the Balanced and Readable wording of 8:13
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats 8:13, so each level keeps its own wording from there.

decisions.choice: the last two lines in the words of 8:13 at each level
alternatives: new wording
decisions.reason: Hosea repeats the line from 8:13; the French repeats it too.

decisions.choice: the last two lines in the words of 8:13: "atakumbuka uovu wao ... kuwaadhibu kwa dhambi zao" (L), "hatia" (B), "mabaya waliyoyatenda ... kuwalipiza" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats 8:13 word for word, so each level reuses the Swahili already drafted there.

decisions.choice: the last two lines in the words of 8:13 at each level: "nhớ lại sự gian ác của chúng ... thăm phạt tội lỗi chúng" (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats 8:13 word for word, so each level reuses the Vietnamese already drafted there.

decisions.choice: The last two lines repeat 8:13 at each level
decisions.reason: The book repeats the line, and Korean keeps the wording of its first use.

source.text: כַּעֲנָבִ֣ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר מָצָ֨אתִי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּבִכּוּרָ֤ה בִתְאֵנָה֙ בְּרֵ֣אשִׁיתָ֔הּ רָאִ֖יתִי אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם הֵ֜מָּה בָּ֣אוּ בַֽעַל־פְּע֗וֹר וַיִּנָּֽזְרוּ֙ לַבֹּ֔שֶׁת וַיִּהְי֥וּ שִׁקּוּצִ֖ים כְּאָהֳבָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like an early fig on a fig tree at its beginning I saw your fathers. They came [to] Baal-peor, and they dedicated themselves to the shame, and they became detestable things like their love.

en.L: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; \q like an early fig on a fig tree in its first [season] \q I saw {{gender:your ancestors|your fathers}}. \q They came [to] Baal of Peor and dedicated themselves to the shame, \q and they became detestable like what they loved.
en.B: Like grapes in the desert, I found Israel; \q like the first ripe fruit on the fig tree in its first season, \q I saw {{gender:your ancestors|your fathers}}. \q But they came to the Baal of Peor and dedicated themselves to the Shameful One, \q and they became as detestable as the thing they loved.
en.R: Finding Israel was like finding grapes in the desert. \q Seeing {{gender:your ancestors|your fathers}} was like seeing the first figs of the season. \q But they came to Baal, the god of Peor, and gave themselves to that shameful god. \q They became as disgusting as the idol they loved.

es.L: Como uvas en el desierto hallé a Israel; \q como breva en la higuera en su primera [cosecha] \q vi a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}. \q Ellos fueron a Baal-peor y se consagraron a la vergüenza, \q y se hicieron abominables como lo que amaban.
es.B: Como uvas en el desierto encontré a Israel; \q como los primeros frutos de la higuera en su primera temporada \q vi a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}. \q Pero ellos fueron a Baal-peor y se consagraron al Vergonzoso, \q y se volvieron tan detestables como aquello que amaban.
es.R: Encontrar a Israel fue como encontrar uvas en el desierto. \q Ver a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} fue como ver los primeros higos de la temporada. \q Pero fueron a Baal, el dios de Peor, y se entregaron a ese dios vergonzoso. \q Se volvieron tan repugnantes como el ídolo que amaban.

fr.L: Comme des raisins dans le désert j’ai trouvé Israël ; \q comme une figue précoce sur un figuier, à sa première [saison], \q j’ai vu {{gender:vos ancêtres|vos pères}}. \q Eux sont venus [à] Baal-Peor et se sont consacrés à la honte, \q et ils sont devenus abominables comme ce qu’ils aimaient.
fr.B: Comme des raisins dans le désert, j’ai trouvé Israël ; \q comme les premiers fruits du figuier à sa première saison, \q j’ai vu {{gender:vos ancêtres|vos pères}}. \q Mais ils sont venus au Baal de Peor et se sont consacrés à la Honte, \q et ils sont devenus aussi abominables que ce qu’ils aimaient.
fr.R: Trouver Israël, c’était comme trouver des raisins dans le désert. \q Voir {{gender:vos ancêtres|vos pères}}, c’était comme voir les premières figues de la saison. \q Mais ils sont venus à Baal, le dieu de Peor, et ils se sont donnés à ce dieu honteux. \q Ils sont devenus aussi dégoûtants que l’idole qu’ils aimaient.

sw.L: Kama zabibu jangwani nilimpata Israeli; \q kama tini ya kwanza juu ya mtini katika [msimu] wake wa kwanza \q niliwaona mababu zenu. \q Wao walikuja [kwa] Baali wa Peori, wakajiweka wakfu kwa ile aibu, \q nao wakawa wa kuchukiza kama kile walichokipenda.
sw.B: Kama zabibu jangwani, nilimpata Israeli; \q kama matunda ya kwanza ya mtini katika msimu wake wa kwanza, \q niliwaona mababu zenu. \q Lakini walikuja kwa Baali wa Peori, wakajiweka wakfu kwa yule Mwenye Aibu, \q nao wakawa wa kuchukiza kama kile walichokipenda.
sw.R: Kumpata Israeli kulikuwa kama kupata zabibu jangwani. \q Kuwaona mababu zenu kulikuwa kama kuona tini za kwanza za msimu. \q Lakini walikuja kwa Baali, mungu wa Peori, wakajitoa kwa mungu huyo wa aibu. \q Wakawa wa kuchukiza kama sanamu waliyoipenda.

vi.L: Như những chùm nho trong hoang mạc, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã gặp Y-sơ-ra-ên; \q như trái vả đầu mùa trên cây vả trong [mùa] đầu tiên của nó, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy tổ tiên các ngươi. \q Chúng đã đến [với] Ba-anh Phê-ô và hiến mình cho sự xấu hổ, \q và chúng trở nên ghê tởm như điều chúng yêu thích.
vi.B: Như gặp được những chùm nho trong hoang mạc, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã gặp Y-sơ-ra-ên; \q như trái chín đầu tiên trên cây vả vào mùa đầu, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy tổ tiên các ngươi. \q Nhưng chúng đã đến với Ba-anh Phê-ô và hiến mình cho Kẻ Đáng Hổ Thẹn, \q và chúng trở nên ghê tởm như vật chúng yêu thích.
vi.R: Ta tìm được Y-sơ-ra-ên như tìm được nho giữa sa mạc. \q Ta thấy tổ tiên các ngươi như thấy những trái vả đầu mùa. \q Nhưng chúng đã đến với Ba-anh, thần của Phê-ô, và dâng mình cho thần đáng hổ thẹn ấy. \q Chúng trở nên ghê tởm như thần tượng chúng yêu thích.

ko.L: 광야의 포도송이처럼 내가 이스라엘을 만났고, \q 무화과나무의 첫 철에 맺힌 첫 열매처럼 \q 내가 너희 조상들을 보았다. \q 그러나 그들은 바알브올에 이르러 그 수치에게 몸을 바쳤고, \q 그들이 사랑한 것처럼 혐오스럽게 되었다.
ko.B: 광야에서 포도송이를 만난 것처럼 나는 이스라엘을 만났다. \q 무화과나무에 처음 맺힌 첫 열매를 보듯이 \q 나는 너희 조상들을 보았다. \q 그러나 그들은 브올의 바알에게 가서 그 수치스러운 신에게 몸을 바쳤고, \q 그들이 사랑한 것처럼 역겨운 자들이 되었다.
ko.R: 내가 이스라엘을 찾은 것은 사막에서 포도송이를 찾은 것과 같았다. \q 너희 조상들을 본 것은 그해 처음 익은 무화과를 본 것과 같았다. \q 그러나 그들은 브올의 신 바알에게 가서 그 부끄러운 신에게 자기를 바쳤다. \q 그들은 자기들이 사랑한 우상처럼 역겨운 자들이 되었다.

decisions.choice: like grapes in the wilderness, like the first figs: Israel was God's delight at the start
decisions.reason: Grapes found in the desert would be a surprise and a joy to a traveler, and the first ripe figs of the season were a prized treat (Isaiah 28:4; Micah 7:1). So the LORD speaks of the time when he first found Israel in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: they came to Baal of Peor: Israel's worship of Baal in Numbers 25
decisions.reason: At Shittim, just before entering the land, Israel joined in the sacrifices of Moab's gods and "yoked itself to Baal of Peor", and a plague struck the people (Numbers 25:1-9; compare Deuteronomy 4:3; Psalm 106:28). Peor was a mountain in Moab, and Baal of Peor the god worshiped there. Hosea traces Israel's love of Baal back to that first fall, at the very start of its life in the land.

decisions.choice: they dedicated themselves: gave themselves wholly to the god
decisions.reason: The verb belongs to the same family as the word Nazirite, a person set apart to the LORD by a vow (Numbers 6:2-12). Israel set itself apart for Baal instead.

decisions.choice: the shame: a scornful name for Baal
decisions.reason: "Shame" stands in place of Baal's name, as in Jeremiah 3:24 and 11:13, where it is parallel to Baal. The same change appears in names: Saul's son Eshbaal (1 Chronicles 8:33) is called Ish-bosheth, "man of shame", in 2 Samuel 2:8.

decisions.choice: they became detestable like what they loved: they became like their idol
alternatives: they became as detestable as their love (their lust) was
decisions.reason: "Detestable things" is a word for idols (Jeremiah 4:1). Israel became as loathsome as the god it loved, as Psalm 115:8 says that idol-makers become like their idols, and 2 Kings 17:15 that Israel followed worthless things and became worthless.

decisions.choice: the Baal of Peor ... the Shameful One (B); Baal, the god of Peor ... that shameful god (R)
decisions.reason: The name follows Numbers 25:3 at each level: "Baal of Peor" (Literal), "the Baal of Peor" (Balanced), "Baal, the god of Peor" (Readable). Balanced capitalizes "the Shameful One" because it stands for a god's name (m4); Readable says plainly that it is a god.

decisions.choice: "Baal-peor" (L, B); "Baal, el dios de Peor" (R); "la vergüenza" (L), "el Vergonzoso" (B), "ese dios vergonzoso" (R)
decisions.reason: The place and god of Numbers 25 as published in Spanish; Hosea's scornful name for Baal is kept at each level as the English levels have it.

decisions.choice: "[[sus padres|vuestros padres]]" (L); "[[sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados]]" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" is plural. Spanish "padres" and "antepasados" already include women, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: "Baali wa Peori" (L, B), "Baali, mungu wa Peori" (R), as Numbers 25:3; "ile aibu" (L), "yule Mwenye Aibu" (B), "mungu huyo wa aibu" (R)
decisions.reason: The name follows the published Numbers 25:3 at each level; Balanced capitalises the title because it stands for the god's name, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Ba-anh Phê-ô" (L, B), "Ba-anh, thần của Phê-ô" (R), as Numbers 25:3; "sự xấu hổ" (L), "Kẻ Đáng Hổ Thẹn" (B), "thần đáng hổ thẹn ấy" (R)
decisions.reason: The name follows the published Numbers 25:3 at each level; Balanced capitalises the title because it stands for the god's name, as the English does. "tổ tiên" already covers men and women, so no gender span.

decisions.choice: "바알브올" (L), "브올의 바알" (B, R); *bosheth* "그 수치" (L), "그 수치스러운 신" (B), "그 부끄러운 신" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms of Deuteronomy 4:3; the scornful name for Baal is translated so the insult stays visible.

decisions.choice: "너희 조상들" with no gender span
alternatives: "{{gender:조상들|아버지들}}"
decisions.reason: Korean "조상" already means ancestors of both sexes, so the English gender span has no second wording in Korean.

source.text: אֶפְרַ֕יִם כָּע֖וֹף יִתְעוֹפֵ֣ף כְּבוֹדָ֑ם מִלֵּדָ֥ה וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן וּמֵהֵרָיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Ephraim, like the bird will fly away their glory, from birth and from womb and from conception.

en.L: Ephraim — like a bird their glory will fly away, \q without birth, and without womb, and without conception.
en.B: As for Ephraim, their glory will fly away like a bird: \q no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
en.R: The glory of Ephraim will fly away like a bird. \q No babies will be born. No women will become pregnant. No children will be conceived.

es.L: Efraín: como un ave volará su gloria, \q sin nacimiento, y sin vientre, y sin concepción.
es.B: En cuanto a Efraín, su gloria volará como un ave: \q no habrá nacimiento, ni embarazo, ni concepción.
es.R: La gloria de Efraín se irá volando como un pájaro. \q No nacerán bebés. Ninguna mujer quedará embarazada. No se concebirán hijos.

fr.L: Éphraïm — comme l’oiseau leur gloire s’envolera, \q sans naissance, et sans grossesse, et sans conception.
fr.B: Quant à Éphraïm, sa gloire s’envolera comme un oiseau : \q plus de naissance, plus de grossesse, plus de conception.
fr.R: La gloire d’Éphraïm s’envolera comme un oiseau. \q Aucun bébé ne naîtra. Aucune femme ne sera enceinte. Aucun enfant ne sera conçu.

sw.L: Efraimu — kama ndege utukufu wao utaruka mbali, \q pasipo kuzaliwa, na pasipo tumbo, na pasipo kutunga mimba.
sw.B: Kuhusu Efraimu, utukufu wao utaruka kama ndege: \q hakuna kuzaa, hakuna kuwa na mimba, hakuna kutunga mimba.
sw.R: Utukufu wa Efraimu utaruka kama ndege. \q Hakuna mtoto atakayezaliwa. Hakuna mwanamke atakayekuwa na mimba. Hakuna mimba itakayotungwa.

vi.L: Ép-ra-im — như chim, vinh quang của chúng sẽ bay đi, \q không còn sinh nở, không còn dạ con, không còn thụ thai.
vi.B: Còn Ép-ra-im, vinh quang của chúng sẽ bay mất như chim: \q không sinh nở, không mang thai, không thụ thai.
vi.R: Vinh quang của Ép-ra-im sẽ bay mất như một con chim. \q Sẽ không có em bé nào chào đời. Không người nữ nào mang thai. Không đứa trẻ nào được thụ thai.

ko.L: 에브라임, 그들의 영광이 새처럼 날아갈 것이니, \q 출산도 없고 임신도 없고 잉태도 없을 것이다.
ko.B: 에브라임은 그 영광이 새처럼 날아가 버릴 것이다. \q 아이를 낳는 일도, 임신하는 일도, 잉태하는 일도 없을 것이다.
ko.R: 에브라임의 영광은 새처럼 날아가 버릴 것이다. \q 아기가 태어나지 않고, 임신하는 여자도 없고, 아이가 생기지도 않을 것이다.

decisions.choice: their glory: Ephraim's abundance, above all its children
decisions.reason: The name Ephraim recalls "fruitful" (Genesis 41:52), and Ephraim's glory was its many children and its strength. Like a bird that is there one moment and gone the next, that glory will fly away. In 10:5 the "glory" of the calf idol also goes into exile.

decisions.choice: no birth, no pregnancy, no conception: life cut off at every stage
decisions.reason: Each noun has "from", in the sense "without". The list runs backward from birth to pregnancy to conception: there will be no children at all. The fertility the people sought from Baal will fail.

decisions.choice: As for Ephraim (B); The glory of Ephraim (R)
decisions.reason: Ephraim stands first in the Hebrew, outside the sentence. Balanced keeps it first with "As for"; Readable joins it to "glory".

source.text: כִּ֤י אִם־יְגַדְּלוּ֙ אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וְשִׁכַּלְתִּ֖ים מֵֽאָדָ֑ם כִּֽי־גַם־א֥וֹי לָהֶ֖ם בְּשׂוּרִ֥י מֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For if they bring up their children, and I will bereave them from a human; for also woe to them when I turn away from them.

en.L: For even if they bring up their children, \q I will bereave them [until] no one [is left]; \q for indeed woe to them when I turn away from them!
en.B: Even if they raise children, \q I will take them until no one is left. \q Yes, woe to them when I turn away from them!
en.R: Even if they raise children, \q I will take those children from them until none are left. \q How terrible it will be for them when I turn away from them!

es.L: Porque aunque críen a sus hijos, \q yo los dejaré sin ellos [hasta que] no [quede] nadie; \q ¡porque ay de ellos también cuando me aparte de ellos!
es.B: Aunque críen hijos, \q se los quitaré hasta que no quede ninguno. \q ¡Sí, ay de ellos cuando me aparte de ellos!
es.R: Aunque críen hijos, \q se los quitaré hasta que no quede ninguno. \q ¡Qué terrible será para ellos cuando me aparte de ellos!

fr.L: Car même s’ils élèvent leurs enfants, \q je les en priverai [jusqu’à ce qu’il ne reste] personne ; \q car oui, malheur à eux quand je me détournerai d’eux !
fr.B: Même s’ils élèvent des enfants, \q je les leur enlèverai jusqu’au dernier. \q Oui, malheur à eux quand je me détournerai d’eux !
fr.R: Même s’ils élèvent des enfants, \q je leur enlèverai ces enfants jusqu’au dernier. \q Quel malheur pour eux quand je me détournerai d’eux !

sw.L: Kwa maana hata wakiwalea watoto wao, \q nitawanyang'anya [hata] asibaki mtu; \q kwa maana kweli ole wao nitakapowaacha!
sw.B: Hata wakilea watoto, \q nitawachukua hadi asibaki hata mmoja. \q Naam, ole wao nitakapowaacha!
sw.R: Hata wakilea watoto, \q nitawanyang'anya watoto hao mpaka wasibaki hata mmoja. \q Itakuwa vibaya mno kwao nitakapowaacha!

vi.L: Vì dù chúng nuôi lớn con cái mình, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ làm chúng mất con [đến nỗi] không còn một người; \q vì thật, khốn cho chúng khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lìa bỏ chúng!
vi.B: Dù chúng có nuôi con cái, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ cất chúng đi cho đến khi không còn ai. \q Phải, khốn cho chúng khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} quay mặt khỏi chúng!
vi.R: Dù chúng có nuôi con cái, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cất những đứa con ấy khỏi chúng cho đến khi không còn đứa nào. \q Thật khủng khiếp cho chúng khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} quay lưng với chúng!

ko.L: 그들이 자식들을 기른다 해도 \q 내가 그들을 빼앗아 한 사람도 [남지] 않게 하겠다. \q 내가 그들을 떠나면 참으로 그들에게 화가 있다!
ko.B: 그들이 자식을 기른다 해도 \q 내가 그 자식들을 빼앗아 한 사람도 남지 않게 하겠다. \q 내가 그들에게서 떠날 때, 그들에게 화가 있다!
ko.R: 그들이 자식을 기른다 해도 \q 나는 그 자식들을 빼앗아 하나도 남지 않게 하겠다. \q 내가 그들에게서 등을 돌릴 때, 그들에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다!

decisions.choice: I will bereave them until no one is left
decisions.reason: "Bereave" is used of parents who lose their children. "From a human" means until there is no one left. Even the children who grow up will be taken.

decisions.choice: woe to them when I turn away from them: God's absence is the worst of the punishments
decisions.reason: The greatest woe is that God himself departs. In 5:6 the people seek the LORD and do not find him, because he has withdrawn from them, and in 5:15 he returns to his place until they seek him. The word for "turn away" is spelled unusually here, but the sense fits the context.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for them
decisions.reason: Readable renders the cry "woe" as the prophets' settled wording does.

source.text: אֶפְרַ֛יִם כַּאֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֥יתִי לְצ֖וֹר שְׁתוּלָ֣ה בְנָוֶ֑ה וְאֶפְרַ֕יִם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶל־הֹרֵ֖ג בָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Ephraim, as I have seen, [is] to Tyre, planted in a pasture; and Ephraim [is] to bring out to [one] killing his children.

en.L: Ephraim, as I have seen, [was] like Tyre, planted in a meadow; \q but Ephraim [is] to bring out his children to the killer.
en.B: Ephraim, as I have seen, was like Tyre, set in a pleasant meadow; \q but Ephraim will lead out his children to the killer.
en.R: I have seen Ephraim planted in a good place, like the city of Tyre. \q But the people of Ephraim will have to bring their children out to be killed.

es.L: Efraín, según he visto, [era] como Tiro, plantada en un prado; \q pero Efraín ha de sacar a sus hijos al que los mata.
es.B: Efraín, según he visto, era como Tiro, plantada en un prado agradable; \q pero Efraín sacará a sus hijos al matadero.
es.R: He visto a Efraín plantado en un buen lugar, como la ciudad de Tiro. \q Pero el pueblo de Efraín tendrá que sacar a sus hijos para que los maten.

fr.L: Éphraïm, comme je l’ai vu, [était] comme Tyr, planté dans une prairie ; \q mais Éphraïm [doit] faire sortir ses enfants vers le tueur.
fr.B: Éphraïm, comme je l’ai vu, était comme Tyr, établi dans une belle prairie ; \q mais Éphraïm mènera ses enfants au tueur.
fr.R: J’ai vu Éphraïm planté dans un bon endroit, comme la ville de Tyr. \q Mais les gens d’Éphraïm devront amener leurs enfants pour qu’on les tue.

sw.L: Efraimu, kama nilivyoona, [alikuwa] kama Tiro, aliyepandwa katika malisho; \q lakini Efraimu [atalazimika] kuwatoa watoto wake kwa mwuaji.
sw.B: Efraimu, kama nilivyoona, alikuwa kama Tiro, aliyewekwa katika malisho mazuri; \q lakini Efraimu atawapeleka watoto wake kwa mwuaji.
sw.R: Nimemwona Efraimu amepandwa mahali pazuri, kama mji wa Tiro. \q Lakini watu wa Efraimu watalazimika kuwatoa watoto wao wauawe.

vi.L: Ép-ra-im, như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy, [giống] như Ty-rơ, được trồng nơi đồng cỏ; \q nhưng Ép-ra-im [phải] dẫn con cái mình ra cho kẻ giết người.
vi.B: Ép-ra-im, như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thấy, giống như Ty-rơ, được đặt giữa đồng cỏ tươi đẹp; \q nhưng Ép-ra-im sẽ dẫn con cái mình ra cho kẻ giết người.
vi.R: Ta đã thấy Ép-ra-im được trồng ở một nơi tốt đẹp, như thành Ty-rơ. \q Nhưng dân Ép-ra-im sẽ phải đem con cái mình ra cho người ta giết.

ko.L: 내가 보니, 에브라임은 풀밭에 심긴 두로와 같았다. \q 그러나 에브라임은 자기 자식들을 살인자에게 끌어내야 한다.
ko.B: 내가 보니, 에브라임은 아름다운 풀밭에 자리 잡은 두로와 같았다. \q 그러나 에브라임은 자기 자식들을 살인자에게 끌어내게 될 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 에브라임이 두로 성처럼 좋은 곳에 심긴 것을 보았다. \q 그러나 에브라임 백성은 자식들을 끌어내어 죽게 해야 할 것이다.

decisions.choice: Ephraim, as I have seen, was like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place
alternatives: Ephraim, as I have seen, has made his sons a prey (the Greek)
decisions.reason: The first half of the verse is one of the hardest lines in Hosea. As the Hebrew is vowelled, it compares Ephraim to Tyre, set in a fine place. The Greek translation (the Septuagint) reads the same letters as "they have set out their children for prey", which makes the two halves say the same thing. The Hebrew is followed here, and the contrast it makes (a fine setting, a terrible end) suits the verse.

decisions.choice: Tyre: the rich trading city of Phoenicia
decisions.reason: Tyre, on the Mediterranean coast north of Israel, was famous for its wealth and its strong position (Ezekiel 27-28). Ephraim too had been set in a rich land.

decisions.choice: Ephraim must bring out his children to the killer
decisions.reason: "Ephraim [is] to bring out" expresses what must happen. The parents will lead their own children out to death in war. The verse leads into verse 14.

source.text: תֵּן־לָהֶ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מַה־תִּתֵּ֑ן תֵּן־לָהֶם֙ רֶ֣חֶם מַשְׁכִּ֔יל וְשָׁדַ֖יִם צֹמְקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Give to them, Yahweh — what will you give? Give to them a miscarrying womb and breasts drying up.

en.L: Give to them, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} — what will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give? \q Give to them a miscarrying womb \q and dry breasts.
en.B: Give them, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} — what should {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give them? \q Give them wombs that miscarry \q and breasts that are dry.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, give them — what should {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give them? \q Give them wombs that lose their babies \q and breasts with no milk.

es.L: Dales, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿qué les darás? \q Dales un vientre que aborte \q y pechos secos.
es.B: Dales, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿qué les vas a dar? \q Dales vientres que aborten \q y pechos secos.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, dales... ¿qué les vas a dar? \q Dales vientres que pierdan a sus bebés \q y pechos sin leche.

fr.L: Donne-leur, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} — que donneras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? \q Donne-leur un ventre qui avorte \q et des seins desséchés.
fr.B: Donne-leur, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} — que dois-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} leur donner ? \q Donne-leur des ventres qui avortent \q et des seins desséchés.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, donne-leur — que dois-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} leur donner ? \q Donne-leur des ventres qui perdent leurs bébés \q et des seins sans lait.

sw.L: Uwape, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} — utawapa nini? \q Uwape tumbo linaloharibu mimba \q na matiti yaliyokauka.
sw.B: Uwape, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} — uwape nini? \q Uwape matumbo yanayoharibu mimba \q na matiti yaliyokauka.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uwape — uwape nini? \q Uwape matumbo yanayopoteza watoto \q na matiti yasiyo na maziwa.

vi.L: Xin ban cho chúng, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} — {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ban gì? \q Xin ban cho chúng dạ con hay sẩy thai \q và bầu vú khô cạn.
vi.B: Xin ban cho chúng, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} — {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nên ban cho chúng điều gì? \q Xin ban cho chúng những dạ con sẩy thai \q và những bầu vú khô cạn.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin ban cho chúng — {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nên ban gì cho chúng? \q Xin cho chúng những dạ con không giữ được thai \q và những bầu vú không có sữa.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 그들에게 주십시오. 무엇을 주시겠습니까? \q 유산하는 태와 \q 마른 젖가슴을 그들에게 주십시오.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 그들에게 주십시오. 무엇을 주셔야 하겠습니까? \q 아이를 잃는 태와 \q 젖이 마른 가슴을 주십시오.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 그들에게 주십시오. 무엇을 주셔야 하겠습니까? \q 아기를 잃는 태를 주십시오. \q 젖이 나오지 않는 가슴을 주십시오.

decisions.choice: Give them, LORD, what will you give? The prophet's prayer, breaking off and starting again
decisions.reason: The prophet begins to pray for his people, stops to ask what he should ask for, and then asks for what seems the lesser evil. The broken sentence shows how hard the prayer is to make.

decisions.choice: a miscarrying womb and dry breasts: Joseph's blessing reversed
decisions.reason: Jacob blessed Joseph, the father of Ephraim, with "blessings of the breasts and of the womb" (Genesis 49:25). The prophet asks for the opposite.

decisions.choice: a prayer for judgment, or for mercy within judgment
alternatives: a plain curse on the people
decisions.reason: After verse 13, where children are led out to be killed, the prophet may be asking for the lighter grief: better that no children be born than that they be born to die. The text gives no reason for the request.

decisions.choice: LORD addressed without "O"; you
decisions.reason: The name addressed in prayer has no "O", as in the Psalms, and "you" spoken to God takes the pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: vocative "SEÑOR" with no "oh"; no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish Psalms and prophets, the LORD addressed directly takes no "oh". The "you" of the prayer is carried by the verb ending ("darás"), so there is no free pronoun for the span.

decisions.choice: The prophet's prayer is in 합쇼체, with the vocative "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여"
decisions.reason: Prophets speak to God in 합쇼체; the vocative takes "여" with no "O", as settled for the divine-name span.

source.text: כָּל־רָעָתָ֤ם בַּגִּלְגָּל֙ כִּֽי־שָׁ֣ם שְׂנֵאתִ֔ים עַ֚ל רֹ֣עַ מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם מִבֵּיתִ֖י אֲגָרְשֵׁ֑ם לֹ֤א אוֹסֵף֙ אַהֲבָתָ֔ם כָּל־שָׂרֵיהֶ֖ם סֹרְרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: All their evil [is] in the Gilgal, for there I hated them; on account of the evil of their deeds, from my house I will drive them out; not I will again love them; all their officials [are] rebels.

en.L: All their evil [is] in Gilgal, for there I hated them; \q because of the evil of their deeds \q I will drive them from my house; \q I will not love them again; \q all their officials [are] rebels.
en.B: All their evil is in Gilgal; there I came to hate them. \q Because of their evil deeds \q I will drive them from my house. \q I will love them no more; \q all their officials are rebels.
en.R: All their evil shows itself at Gilgal. That is where I began to hate them. \q Because of the evil things they do, \q I will drive them out of my house. \q I will not love them any longer. \q All their leaders have turned against me.

es.L: Toda su maldad [está] en Guilgal, porque allí los aborrecí; \q por la maldad de sus obras \q los echaré de mi casa; \q no los amaré más; \q todos sus príncipes [son] rebeldes.
es.B: Toda su maldad está en Guilgal; allí llegué a aborrecerlos. \q Por sus malas obras \q los echaré de mi casa. \q No los amaré más; \q todos sus jefes son rebeldes.
es.R: Toda su maldad se ve en Guilgal. Allí comencé a aborrecerlos. \q Por las cosas malas que hacen, \q los echaré de mi casa. \q Ya no los amaré más. \q Todos sus dirigentes se han puesto en mi contra.

fr.L: Toute leur méchanceté [est] à Guilgal, car là je les ai haïs ; \q à cause de la méchanceté de leurs actions \q je les chasserai de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison ; \q je ne les aimerai plus ; \q tous leurs chefs [sont] des rebelles.
fr.B: Toute leur méchanceté est à Guilgal ; c’est là que je me suis mis à les haïr. \q À cause de leurs mauvaises actions, \q je les chasserai de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison. \q Je ne les aimerai plus ; \q tous leurs chefs sont des rebelles.
fr.R: Toute leur méchanceté se montre à Guilgal. C’est là que j’ai commencé à les haïr. \q À cause du mal qu’ils font, \q je les chasserai de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison. \q Je ne les aimerai plus. \q Tous leurs dirigeants se sont révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Uovu wao wote [uko] Gilgali, kwa maana huko niliwachukia; \q kwa sababu ya uovu wa matendo yao \q nitawafukuza kutoka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q sitawapenda tena; \q wakuu wao wote [ni] waasi.
sw.B: Uovu wao wote uko Gilgali; huko ndiko nilikoanza kuwachukia. \q Kwa sababu ya matendo yao maovu \q nitawafukuza kutoka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Sitawapenda tena; \q wakuu wao wote ni waasi.
sw.R: Uovu wao wote unaonekana huko Gilgali. Huko ndiko nilikoanza kuwachukia. \q Kwa sababu ya mambo maovu wanayoyatenda, \q nitawafukuza kutoka nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Sitawapenda tena. \q Viongozi wao wote wameniasi.

vi.L: Mọi điều ác của chúng [đều] ở tại Ghinh-ganh, vì tại đó {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ghét chúng; \q vì việc làm gian ác của chúng \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đuổi chúng ra khỏi nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không yêu chúng nữa; \q mọi quan chức của chúng [đều là] kẻ phản nghịch.
vi.B: Mọi điều ác của chúng đều ở Ghinh-ganh; tại đó {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã bắt đầu ghét chúng. \q Vì những việc làm gian ác của chúng, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đuổi chúng ra khỏi nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta sẽ không yêu chúng nữa; \q mọi quan chức của chúng đều là kẻ phản nghịch.
vi.R: Mọi điều ác của chúng đều lộ ra tại Ghinh-ganh. Chính tại đó {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bắt đầu ghét chúng. \q Vì những việc ác chúng làm, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đuổi chúng ra khỏi nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta sẽ không yêu chúng nữa. \q Mọi người lãnh đạo của chúng đều đã chống nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그들의 모든 악이 길갈에 있으니, 내가 거기에서 그들을 미워했다. \q 그들의 행실이 악하므로 \q 내가 그들을 내 집에서 쫓아내겠다. \q 다시는 그들을 사랑하지 않겠다. \q 그들의 고관들은 모두 반역자들이다.
ko.B: 그들의 모든 악이 길갈에 있다. 거기에서 나는 그들을 미워하게 되었다. \q 그들의 악한 행실 때문에 \q 내가 그들을 내 집에서 쫓아내겠다. \q 다시는 그들을 사랑하지 않겠다. \q 그들의 관리들은 모두 반역자들이다.
ko.R: 그들의 악은 길갈에서 다 드러난다. 거기에서 나는 그들을 미워하기 시작했다. \q 그들이 저지른 악한 일 때문에 \q 나는 그들을 내 집에서 쫓아내겠다. \q 더 이상 그들을 사랑하지 않겠다. \q 그들의 지도자들은 모두 나에게 등을 돌렸다.

decisions.choice: Gilgal: a center of worship, and the place where Saul was made king
decisions.reason: Gilgal, near Jericho, was where Israel first camped in the land (Joshua 4:19-20). By Hosea's time it was a shrine where sacrifices were offered (4:15; 12:12; Amos 4:4; 5:5), and it was where Saul was made king (1 Samuel 11:15). "All their evil" there may point to its worship or to the kingship; Hosea condemns both.

decisions.choice: hated, driven out of my house, not loved again: the language of a husband sending away his wife
decisions.reason: "Hate" is used of a husband who turns against his wife (Deuteronomy 24:3), and "drive out" of a woman sent away in divorce (Leviticus 21:7). God's "house" is his land and household (8:1). The picture of Israel as the unfaithful wife (chapter 2) is turned into a sentence of divorce.

decisions.choice: their officials are rebels: a play on two similar words
decisions.reason: "Their officials" and "rebels" sound alike in Hebrew (sarehem sorerim). Isaiah 1:23 uses the same pair of words of Jerusalem's leaders.

decisions.choice: officials (L, B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for a royal officer is "officials", as in the other prophets. Readable says "leaders".

source.text: הֻכָּ֣ה אֶפְרַ֔יִם שָׁרְשָׁ֥ם יָבֵ֖שׁ פְּרִ֣י בַֽל־יַעֲשׂ֑וּן גַּ֚ם כִּ֣י יֵֽלֵד֔וּן וְהֵמַתִּ֖י מַחֲמַדֵּ֥י בִטְנָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Struck [is] Ephraim; their root has dried up; fruit not they will produce; even if they give birth, and I will put to death [the] precious [ones] of their womb.

en.L: Ephraim is struck; \q their root has dried up; they will not produce fruit; \q even if they give birth, \q I will put to death the precious [ones] of their womb.
en.B: Ephraim is struck down; \q their root has dried up, and they will bear no fruit. \q Even if they give birth, \q I will put to death the dear children of their womb.
en.R: Ephraim is like a plant that has been struck down. \q Its roots have dried up, and it will grow no fruit. \q Even if they have babies, \q I will put to death the children they love.

es.L: Efraín está herido; \q su raíz se ha secado; no darán fruto; \q aunque den a luz, \q yo haré morir los [hijos] amados de su vientre.
es.B: Efraín ha sido herido; \q su raíz se ha secado, y no dará fruto. \q Aunque den a luz, \q haré morir a los hijos queridos de su vientre.
es.R: Efraín es como una planta que ha sido derribada. \q Sus raíces se han secado, y no dará fruto. \q Aunque tengan bebés, \q haré morir a los hijos que aman.

fr.L: Éphraïm est frappé ; \q leur racine a séché ; ils ne produiront pas de fruit ; \q même s’ils enfantent, \q je ferai mourir les [enfants] chéris de leur ventre.
fr.B: Éphraïm est abattu ; \q leur racine a séché, ils ne porteront plus de fruit. \q Même s’ils ont des enfants, \q je ferai mourir les enfants chéris de leur ventre.
fr.R: Éphraïm est comme une plante qui a été abattue. \q Ses racines ont séché, et elle ne donnera plus de fruit. \q Même si les gens ont des bébés, \q je ferai mourir les enfants qu’ils aiment.

sw.L: Efraimu amepigwa; \q mzizi wao umekauka; hawatazaa matunda; \q hata wakizaa, \q nitawaua [watoto] wapendwa wa tumbo lao.
sw.B: Efraimu amepigwa chini; \q mzizi wao umekauka, nao hawatazaa matunda. \q Hata wakizaa, \q nitawaua watoto wapendwa wa tumbo lao.
sw.R: Efraimu ni kama mmea uliopigwa ukaanguka. \q Mizizi yake imekauka, na hautazaa matunda. \q Hata watu wakipata watoto, \q nitawaua watoto wanaowapenda.

vi.L: Ép-ra-im bị đánh; \q rễ của chúng đã khô héo; chúng sẽ không sinh trái; \q dù chúng có sinh nở, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ giết [những đứa con] quý báu từ lòng chúng.
vi.B: Ép-ra-im bị đánh gục; \q rễ của chúng đã khô héo, chúng sẽ không còn sinh trái. \q Dù chúng có sinh con, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ giết những đứa con yêu quý chúng đã cưu mang.
vi.R: Ép-ra-im như một cây bị đánh gục. \q Rễ nó đã khô héo, và nó sẽ không ra trái nữa. \q Dù chúng có sinh con, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ giết những đứa con chúng yêu thương.

ko.L: 에브라임이 얻어맞아 \q 그들의 뿌리가 말랐으니, 열매를 맺지 못할 것이다. \q 그들이 아이를 낳는다 해도 \q 내가 그들의 태의 귀한 [자식들을] 죽이겠다.
ko.B: 에브라임은 얻어맞아 쓰러졌다. \q 그 뿌리가 말라 버렸으니 열매를 맺지 못할 것이다. \q 그들이 아이를 낳는다 해도 \q 내가 그들이 낳은 귀한 자식들을 죽이겠다.
ko.R: 에브라임은 병들어 쓰러진 나무와 같다. \q 뿌리가 말라 버려서 열매를 맺지 못할 것이다. \q 그들이 아기를 낳는다 해도 \q 나는 그들이 사랑하는 자식들을 죽게 하겠다.

decisions.choice: Ephraim is struck: like a plant blighted at the root
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a plant struck down by heat or a worm (Psalm 102:5; Jonah 4:7). Ephraim is pictured as a tree whose root has dried up.

decisions.choice: Ephraim ... fruit: a play on the name
decisions.reason: The name Ephraim sounds like the word for fruit and was explained as "God has made me fruitful" (Genesis 41:52). The fruitful one will bear no fruit, and the children it does bear will die.

decisions.choice: the precious ones of their womb: their dear children
decisions.reason: "Precious things" is used in verse 6 of silver treasures. Here it means the children they love.

decisions.choice: like a plant
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture of a plant explicit (m1).

source.text: יִמְאָסֵ֣ם אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ ל֑וֹ וְיִהְי֥וּ נֹדְדִ֖ים בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Will reject them my God, for not they have listened to him; and they will be wanderers among the nations.

en.L: My God will reject them, \q because they have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q and they will be wanderers among the nations.
en.B: My God will reject them \q because they have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and they will wander among the nations.
en.R: My God will reject them \q because they have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q They will wander from nation to nation.

es.L: Mi Dios los rechazará, \q porque no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} han escuchado; \q y andarán errantes entre las naciones.
es.B: Mi Dios los rechazará \q porque no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} han escuchado, \q y andarán errantes entre las naciones.
es.R: Mi Dios los rechazará \q porque no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} han obedecido. \q Andarán de nación en nación.

fr.L: Mon Dieu les rejettera, \q car ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont pas écouté ; \q et ils seront errants parmi les nations.
fr.B: Mon Dieu les rejettera \q parce qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont pas écouté, \q et ils erreront parmi les nations.
fr.R: Mon Dieu les rejettera \q parce qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont pas obéi. \q Ils erreront de nation en nation.

sw.L: Mungu wangu atawakataa, \q kwa sababu hawakumsikiliza; \q nao watakuwa watu wa kutangatanga kati ya mataifa.
sw.B: Mungu wangu atawakataa \q kwa sababu hawakumsikiliza, \q nao watatangatanga kati ya mataifa.
sw.R: Mungu wangu atawakataa \q kwa sababu hawakumtii. \q Watatangatanga kutoka taifa hadi taifa.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời của tôi sẽ loại bỏ chúng, \q vì chúng không nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q và chúng sẽ thành kẻ lang thang giữa các dân tộc.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời của tôi sẽ loại bỏ chúng \q vì chúng đã không nghe lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và chúng sẽ lang thang giữa các dân tộc.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời của tôi sẽ loại bỏ chúng \q vì chúng đã không vâng lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Chúng sẽ lưu lạc từ nước này sang nước khác.

ko.L: 나의 하나님께서 그들을 버리실 것이다. \q 그들이 그분의 말씀을 듣지 않았기 때문이다. \q 그들은 민족들 가운데서 떠돌이가 될 것이다.
ko.B: 나의 하나님께서 그들을 버리실 것이다. \q 그들이 그분께 귀를 기울이지 않았기 때문이다. \q 그들은 민족들 가운데서 떠돌아다닐 것이다.
ko.R: 나의 하나님께서 그들을 버리실 것이다. \q 그들이 그분께 순종하지 않았기 때문이다. \q 그들은 이 나라 저 나라로 떠돌아다닐 것이다.

decisions.choice: my God: the prophet speaks
decisions.reason: The LORD has spoken in the first person in verses 15-16; now the prophet speaks of him as "my God", as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: they have not listened to him: they have not obeyed
decisions.reason: To listen to God, in Hebrew, is to obey him.

decisions.choice: wanderers among the nations: the curse of Cain and of the covenant
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the one used of Cain, condemned to be a restless wanderer (Genesis 4:12, 14), and the covenant warned that a disobedient Israel would be scattered among the nations with no rest (Deuteronomy 28:64-65).

decisions.choice: "나의 하나님께서 … 버리실 것이다": the prophet speaks of God with the honorific
decisions.reason: Here, as in 9:8, the prophet speaks in his own voice ("my God"), so God takes -시- and 께서.
